The guard runs once, inside execute_run, which raises IncompatiblePipelineError on

The detectors a benchmark can compare, with their training capability.

The committed bench specs, with the corpora each one fits.

Read per request rather than cached: unlike ``DETECTORS``, these are files an operator
can edit while the server runs, and a benchmark replaying a spec the YAML no longer
says is the exact class of divergence this endpoint exists to close.

Synchronous by design (see the module docstring). Errors are mapped by *kind*: an
absent corpus is 404 (ask for something else), a corpus/spec mismatch is 422 (the
request is incoherent) — never a 500, because both are ordinary user situations.

BenchSpecSummary.title: BenchSpecSummary
BenchSpecSummary.description:
One shipped benchmark spec, and the corpora it can actually run on.

Published so a UI can run **the committed spec** rather than compose a lookalike. The
dashboard's Evaluate page used to build its own ``PipelineSpec`` from the detectors picked
on screen, which silently dropped the ``assets:`` block and every source and engine
parameter — so the page and the CLI reported different numbers for what read as the same
benchmark (mean true priority 39.46 from ``stub.yaml``, 35.72 from the page's
reconstruction) with nothing on either surface disclosing which spec produced them.

``corpora`` is the join a client would otherwise have to compute: which corpora this spec's
source shape matches (``eval.bench``).

lane_recall.title: Lane Recall
lane_recall.description: Per-lane event recall, derived — it was the seventh stored copy of ``lanes``.

CaseReport.title: CaseReport
CaseReport.description:
One spec's result on one labelled case.

Flat rather than two nested metric objects, deliberately: this is the JSON a CI gate
keys into (``cases[].event_f1``), so the shape is part of the artifact's contract.
``None`` on any ratio means *undefined*, never zero — see ``score.ratio``.

CaseTimeline.title: CaseTimeline
CaseTimeline.description:
Where the faults, detections and alerts actually fell, for one case.

The data behind the timeline chart, and the only part of a report that is about *shape*
rather than *score*. It answers the question a table cannot: a detector with
``det/inc 300`` is fragmenting, but you only *see* what that costs an analyst when the
three lanes are drawn against one clock.

Off by default (``include_timeline``): the report's other job is to be a small, diffable
artifact a CI gate reads, and spans would dominate it.

fetchable.title: Fetchable
fetchable.description: Datasets convertible locally but not shipped; value is how to get them

source_formats.title: Source Formats
source_formats.description: The input shape a spec must declare to benchmark this corpus: one source format per position, in order. A UI composing a spec needs it to build one that fits.

lanes.title: Lanes
lanes.description: The detector lanes this corpus can actually feed. A UI picking detectors needs it: one that consumes none of these lanes is handed no events and scores a row of zeros it never had the chance to earn.

payloads.title: Payloads
payloads.description: The typed lane vocabularies this corpus's events carry (ADR-0035). The lane is necessary and not sufficient: a stub-csv bundle feeds lane 'telemetry' and no payload, so meter_iforest matched on lane, was offered, and discarded every event. A UI must intersect BOTH axes.

error.title: Error

CorpusSummary.title: CorpusSummary
CorpusSummary.description: One corpus as a picker sees it — described without paying to load its readings.

Criticality.title: Criticality
Criticality.description: How much an asset matters — feeds the prioritizer's device weight.

payloads.title: Payloads
payloads.description: The typed lane vocabularies this detector requires an event to carry (ADR-0035). Every one of them must be in the corpus's `payloads` for this detector to judge anything: meter_iforest consumes lane 'telemetry' AND payload 'meter', and a corpus satisfying only the lane hands it events it discards one by one. REQUIRED, unlike CorpusSummary.payloads: an absent field here fails OPEN (every detector passes the filter), which is the permissive silence ADR-0035 removes. Absent on the corpus side fails closed, so that one may default.

DetectorSummary.title: DetectorSummary
DetectorSummary.description:
A benchmarkable detector. ``fittable`` tells the UI whether fit protocols apply.

``lanes`` is *decoded* server-side into bare ``Lane`` values, mirroring
``ModuleInfo.formats``: capability tokens render to wire form only at the API boundary,
so a client never has to know the ``lane:`` prefix scheme (``capabilities.py``). Plural
because ``consumes`` is a set — a detector may legitimately consume more than one lane,
and picking one arbitrarily would misreport it.

``params`` and ``artifact_param`` are the ADR-0022 declaration, carried here so the
Evaluate page needs *one* call rather than joining this against ``/modules``: which
hyperparameters exist (with real defaults, so a form can prefill them), and which
param — if any — names a cached fit. A UI reads the latter to offer "use trained
weights" and "fit from scratch with my own hyperparameters" as two exclusive modes,
instead of letting someone combine them and hit the atomicity error.

LabelledSpec.title: LabelledSpec
LabelledSpec.description:
A spec plus the name it appears under in the report, optionally swept.

``sweep`` maps a detector hyperparameter to the values to vary it across; the server
cross-products them into one labelled spec per combination before evaluating
(ADR-0022). Expanding server-side rather than in the client is what keeps the CLI and
the dashboard producing identical labels and obeying one expansion cap.

Lane.title: Lane
Lane.description: Detection modality — which specialist lane an event or detection belongs to.

LaneCounts.title: LaneCounts
LaneCounts.description:
One lane's tallies — the unit both the point and event levels are really counted in.

Per lane because a lane's instants are its own (``truth.AssetTruth``) and, since ADR-0028
D2, so are its incidents. Pooling these into one set of point counts weights each modality
by **how fast it samples**, which is a corpus-authoring decision masquerading as a
measurement: on ``device_trimodal`` FLOW carries 1,321 of 2,918 clock entries and telemetry
1,440 (the split moves whenever a device profile does — ADR-0028 D5/D7), so a
pooled point precision is a telemetry number wearing a corpus-wide name.

Kept as counts rather than rates so pooling stays addition, the same reason ``Counts``
does — and so ``report._attribution`` can pool per-lane recall across cases instead of
averaging rates, which is the one column ADR-0027 D4 could not reach.

PipelineSpec.title: PipelineSpec
PipelineSpec.description:
The operator-chosen shape of a run: which adapters, over what input source(s), to where.

Deliberately excludes ``database_url`` — *where the database lives* is a deployment
decision, not an operator one (a tenant must never point a run at an arbitrary
database). The Pipeline API accepts a ``PipelineSpec`` and the server supplies
``database_url`` from its environment; the CLI's ``load_config`` produces a full
``PipelineConfig`` directly. ``sinks`` *is* operator-chosen (which stores/deliveries
to fan the result out to); the Postgres sink among them is what reads ``database_url``.

``sources`` is the multi-source ingest list (ADR-0019). A pre-validator desugars the
legacy single-source form (top-level ``source_format``/``normalizer``) into a one-element
``sources`` list, so every config and spec written before multi-source keeps working.

``detection_ids`` is the lineage; more than one entry means corroboration.
Every detection bucket becomes an alert — ranking, not a hidden gate,
decides what analysts look at first (ADR-0003 D3).

SourceSpec.title: SourceSpec
SourceSpec.description:
One input source: which normalizer parses it, asserting its raw format (ADR-0019).

A run ingests a *list* of these, so one run can carry mixed modalities (telemetry CSV
*and* syslog) that pool into the detector lanes. Routing is explicit — the operator (or
source system) tags each source with its ``normalizer``/``source_format``; the pipeline
never sniffs a blob's format (the normalizer double-checks and rejects a mismatch, as a
config error). ``path`` is a loading hint used only by the file-reading CLI to locate a
source's content; the Pipeline API ignores it (content arrives in the request) and the
compatibility guard ignores it (it is not part of the chain's shape).

``params`` configures the normalizer itself, exactly as ``DetectorConfig.params``
configures a detector (ADR-0023 D8). Normalizers were the only one of the four ports
that could not be parameterized — an asymmetry rather than a decision: the builder
hardcoded an empty mapping, while the ``/modules`` catalogue already introspected
normalizer factory signatures for parameters that could never arrive. The flow
normalizer's ``home_networks`` is the first real need. Additive with a default, so
every config file and API request written before this stays valid.

pooled.title: Pooled
pooled.description:
``summary()``, serialized — the headline a CI gate can read without re-pooling.

ADR-0027 left this as a gap: the report carried the per-case counts but no corpus-level
number, so a gate wanting the pooled figure had to sum ``cases[].*`` and divide, which
is a third place that would know how a rate is formed. Exposing the *result* of the one
definition is not a second definition.

pooled_by_lane.title: Pooled By Lane
pooled_by_lane.description: ``rates_by_lane()``, serialized, for the same reason as ``pooled``.

SpecReport.title: SpecReport
SpecReport.description: One benchmarked pipeline spec, across every case in the corpus.
